}}{{Recipe}}

'''Molokhia''' is a popular Egyptian [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] made from the leaves of the jute mallow plant. It is a comforting and flavorful dish that is often enjoyed with rice or bread. Molokhia has a unique texture and a distinct earthy taste, making it a beloved staple in Egyptian cuisine.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] fresh or frozen [[Cookbook:Jute|jute mallow]] (molokhia) leaves
* 4 cups vegetable or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:olive oil|olive oil]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 3 cloves [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:cumin|cumin]]
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:black pepper|Black pepper]] to taste
* Juice of 1 [[Cookbook:lemon|lemon]] (optional)
* Cooked [[Cookbook:rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:bread|bread]] for serving

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Saucepan|Saucepan]]
* Wooden spoon or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* [[Cookbook:Knife|Knife]]
* [[Cookbook:Cutting Board|Cutting board]]
* Serving bowl or plate

== Procedure ==
# If using fresh molokhia leaves, remove any tough stems and wash the leaves thoroughly. If using frozen molokhia, thaw it according to the package instructions.
# In a saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and minced garlic. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] until the onion becomes translucent and the garlic becomes fragrant.
# Add the fresh or thawed molokhia leaves to the saucepan and stir well to combine with the onion and garlic mixture.
# Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth, ensuring that the molokhia leaves are fully submerged.
# Season the soup with ground cumin, salt, and black pepper to taste. Stir to incorporate the spices.
# Bring the soup to a gentle [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], then reduce the heat to low and let it [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 20–30 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together.
# Remove the soup from the heat. Optionally, squeeze the juice of a lemon into the soup and stir well to enhance the flavors.
# Serve the molokhia hot, accompanied by cooked [[Cookbook:rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:bread|bread]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Molokhia is traditionally served with rice or bread. It can be enjoyed as a standalone soup or as part of a larger meal with additional side dishes. Some variations of molokhia include the addition of meat or poultry for added protein.
